To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of carbidopa premedication in adult patients with HH is a useful approach that allows for the visualization of insulinomas in more than 50 % of cases.

CD administration before ¹⁸F-FDOP A injection leads to low ¹⁸-F-FDOPA residual activity in the pancreas, preserving the tumor uptake, with consequent insulinomas detection in more than 50% of adult patients with hypoglycemia and more than 60% of patients with final diagnosis of insulinomas.
18F-FDG PET/CT imaging is increasingly used to work-up patients with neuroendocrinediseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of 18F-FDG PET/CT for the detection of insulinoma.

the study of the effect of the administration of carbidopa (a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor) on the 18F-FDG and 18F-FDAO PET uptake in the pancreas and in the pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour (pNET) in patients with neuroendocrinal syndrome.

the study of the effect of carbidopa on the uptake of the radiotracer 18F-DOPA by the pancreatic gland and its potential to improve the sensitivity of PET/CT for the diagnosis of insulinoma in adult patients with hyperinsulineemic hypoglycemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
18F-FDG PET/CT is still the first line of investigation in adult patients with HH.
18F-FDG PET is the best PET tracer for the diagnosis and localization of insulinomas.
the combination of CD premedication and early acquisition of 18F-FDG PET/CT is the best option to detect insulinomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD premedication is essential for the success of 18F-Fdopa PET imaging of insulinoma.

18F-FDG is the preferred PET radiopharmaceutical for the diagnosis of insulinoma, while 18F-FDOA PET is useful for the diagnosis of neuroendocrine tumour, including insulinoma, in the presence of other tumour sites.
18F-FDG is the preferred tracer for imaging insulinomas, but 18F-FDAO is a reasonable alternative if 18F-FGD is unavailable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD administration is mandatory in 18F-FDAOPA PET imaging of insulinoma.
CD administration before 11C-5-HTP injection is not necessary in the work-up patients with HH and that 11C- 5-HTP PET/CT is a promising tool for localizing insulinomas in adults with HH.
18F-FDG PET/CT should still be the first line of investigation in patients with HH, and 18F-FDOA PET/CT could be reserved to those with inconclusive 18F-FG PET/CT.
